item.title: PHP2Shell Exploitation, Cloudflare Workers AI Data Exposure, and Supply-Chain Fixes
item.content:encoded:
Window: 26 Oct 19:00 → 26 Oct 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

How to patch PHP2Shell with free Aikido Images — Must Read

Critical PHP2Shell RCE flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) are reportedly being exploited, so organizations should immediately upgrade to fixed PHP releases or use Aikido’s backported container images for unsupported PHP versions and redeploy affected containers.

  • PHP2Shell consists of two critical PHP remote-code-execution flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each rated 9.2 under CVSS v4.0.
  • PHP released fixes on October 21 in versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, while PHP 8.1 and older will not receive upstream releases because they are out of support.
  • Cloudflare reports that exploitation of PHP2Shell has started.
  • Aikido provides free patched PHP container images for release lines 5.5 through 8.5, except PHP 8.0, with the PHP2Shell fixes backported for older versions.
  • After switching images, the article recommends rebuilding and redeploying PHP containers, disabling session.upload_progress.enabled, checking public sites with Aikido’s PHP2Shell checker, and looking for signs of compromise.

Technologies: container-platform, package-registry, cloud-platform, web-server

Products: php, aikido-images, amazon-elastic-container-registry, docker, php-fpm, apache-http-server

Vendors: aikido, php, cloudflare, amazon, docker

Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model, and our remediation with SGLang — Should Read

Cloudflare disclosed that a misconfigured KV-cache pool and an SGLang disaggregated-inference bug caused 155 GLM-5.3 Workers AI responses to expose data from recent requests by other customers between August 27 and September 9, 2026. Cloudflare took the model offline, corrected the configuration and engine behavior, restored service, and worked with SGLang on upstream fixes and broader KV-cache safety hardening.

  • Cloudflare disclosed that 155 responses from its GLM-5.3 Workers AI model contained data from other customers’ recent requests between August 27 and September 9, 2026.
  • The exposure occurred only for prompts longer than 681,280 tokens, because the model’s configured 1,048,576-token context window exceeded the capacity of its prefill memory cache.
  • An SGLang disaggregated prefill/decode bug allowed rejected oversized requests to transfer only placeholder data while decode systems read leftover memory pages from earlier requests.
  • Cloudflare disabled the model on September 9, increased the prefill cache capacity to about 2.04 million tokens, patched the inference engine, and restored the model later that day.
  • Cloudflare stated that no other Workers AI model was affected and recommended that disaggregated SGLang operators update to version 0.5.22 or later.

Technologies: cloud-platform, load-balancer

Products: workers-ai, glm-5-3, sglang, mooncake

Vendors: cloudflare, z-ai, radixark, sglang-project, mooncake

eMudhra, Brotli, and the Long Tail of a Security Fix — May Read

Fixing the eMudhra certificate compromise and Brotli flaw requires more than updating Node.js: vulnerable certificate trust paths and bundled decoders may persist across runtimes, applications, and compiled artifacts. Organizations need to inventory what actually shipped, rebuild affected software, and verify that the running application uses the corrected trust store or library.

  • eMudhra disclosed that a flawed key-generation ceremony in April 2025 produced eight intermediate certificate authority private keys that fit within eight bits, making them easy to recover.
  • Chrome and Firefox distributed blocks for the compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates, but other applications may use different certificate stores or verification paths and still trust them.
  • Node.js patched both the eMudhra certificate issue and the Brotli decoding flaw, but updating Node.js does not fix separate bundled or compiled copies in other software.
  • The Brotli flaw, CVE-2026-111497, can corrupt memory when applications decode malicious compressed data and also affected software including Bun, Python Requests installations with Brotli support, and .NET.
  • Organizations should inventory bundled dependencies, rebuild affected artifacts, apply available mitigations, and verify that deployed applications are using corrected decoders and certificate verification settings.

Technologies: browser, operating-system

Products: nodejs, brotli, bun, python-requests, dotnet, golang, firefox, google-chrome, macos

Vendors: emudhra, nodejs, google, oven, microsoft, mozilla, apple, cloudflare

Authorization Differential Testing in Salesforce — Optional

Salesforce authorization should be tested by sending the same request through UI API, GraphQL, and custom Apex, since custom Apex can enforce permissions differently and expose data withheld by native APIs. Review Apex sharing declarations, class API versions, and explicit database access modes—especially for Experience Cloud guest-accessible methods.

  • Authorization Differential Testing compares the same operation for the same user, record, and field across UI API, GraphQL, custom Apex, and other application paths to identify inconsistent access decisions.
  • Salesforce UI API and its GraphQL API enforce the caller’s object permissions, field-level security, and record-sharing access, while custom Apex requires separate review of its authorization behavior.
  • Apex classes using `with sharing` enforce record-level sharing but do not, by themselves, enforce object permissions or field-level security for system-mode database operations.
  • Apex database operations in classes compiled at API version 66 or earlier default to system mode unless user mode is selected, whereas classes compiled at API version 67 or later default to user mode.
  • Experience Cloud guest access to native APIs and to custom Apex methods should be tested separately because guest users may reach different authorization checks through each path.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam

Products: experience-cloud, ui-api, graphql-api, apex, lightning-data-service, lightning-web-runtime

Vendors: salesforce

Socket Threat Intel now shows whether malware campaigns were blocked, detected, or not seen in an organization, with links to the relevant repository scans and Firewall events. The Org Impact view lets teams trace affected package versions to specific repositories, branches, and evidence.

  • Campaign summaries draw on immutable repository scans, pull-request diff scans, and Socket Firewall event traffic.
  • The Org Impact tab lists campaign packages found in an organization, including the repositories and branches containing them and their first and last observed dates.
  • Date links in Org Impact open the associated scan report or matching Socket Firewall events.
  • For campaigns involving multiple packages, Org Impact displays each package and version separately with its own status and first and last seen dates.

Varonis' Takeaways from Forrester’s 2026 Email, Messaging, and Collaboration Security Solutions Landscape Report — Optional

Varonis highlights Forrester’s 2026 email, messaging, and collaboration security landscape, arguing that AI-driven social engineering increasingly crosses channels and exploits trusted communications. The company promotes Varonis Interceptor as a zero-trust defense that analyzes and blocks malicious links before users or AI agents interact with them.

  • Forrester published The Email, Messaging, And Collaboration Security Solutions Landscape, Q4 2026 on October 23, and it includes Varonis Interceptor among 26 notable vendors.
  • The article says attackers use AI to tailor phishing campaigns at scale, while AI agents increasingly read emails, open links and files, and carry out requests for employees.
  • The article states that social-engineering campaigns can move from email into chat threads, shared files, browser tabs, personal accounts, web traffic, and social platforms.
  • Forrester identifies the primary challenge as malicious intent hiding inside legitimate communications, including messages from real colleague mailboxes, familiar vendors, or existing message threads.
  • Varonis says Interceptor tests every message in a sandbox before users or agents interact with it and blocks phishing links from email, collaboration tools, search, ads, and social media.

item.title: LiteLLM Supply-Chain Compromise, PHP CVEs, and Lazarus FlashHole Lead Threat Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 26 Oct 15:00 → 26 Oct 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

LiteLLM Compromise: Coding Agents as the New Insider Risk — Should Read

A leaked master key in an OpenCode agent configuration enabled attackers to steal GitHub tokens, abuse CI workflows to harvest more secrets, and publish the credential-stealing LiteLLM 1.107.0 package. The incident shows that coding agents and unmanaged, long-lived credentials create a major supply-chain risk unless identities are scoped, short-lived, monitored, and kept out of local configs and CI secrets.

  • A master key for LiteLLM’s internal Agent Platform was committed to a public repository in an OpenCode configuration file on May 27 and remained valid for about four and a half months after the commit was removed.
  • On October 10, an attacker used the leaked master key to retrieve managed-agent configurations and obtain a GitHub CLI OAuth token belonging to a LiteLLM GitHub organization owner.
  • The attacker added GitHub Actions workflows that collected and sent repository secrets, including maintainers’ GitHub CLI tokens and database and Redis credentials, to an external webhook service.
  • The poisoned litellm==1.107.0 release was available on PyPI from 11:39 to 13:23 UTC on October 21, 2026, and its Docker images remained available until 14:20 UTC.
  • The malicious package executed code whenever Python started and searched affected machines for cloud credentials, SSH keys, tokens, .env files, shell history, browser passwords, and LLM-provider keys before sending them to an attacker-controlled domain.

Technologies: ci-cd, source-control, package-registry, iam

Products: litellm, opencode, github-actions, github-cli, pypi, docker-hub, github-container-registry, cyera-agent-guardian, cyera-identity

Vendors: litellm, github, docker, opencode, cyera

  • The article stresses that these identity-data associations are investigative leads and not independent proof of wrongdoing.
  • Historical breach records, reused usernames, and other identity associations can help analysts connect and evaluate otherwise fragmented information.

item.title: Infoblox Details Domain Shadowing Abused for Gambling SEO
item.content:encoded:
Window: 26 Oct 11:00 → 26 Oct 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

Borrowed Reputation: Domain Shadowing and Gambling SEO — Should Read

Infoblox uncovered two domain-shadowing operations that abused unauthorized DNS records and subdomain delegations under legitimate school and government domains to host illegal gambling SEO pages. Organizations should monitor DNS changes, especially unexpected CNAMEs, NS delegations, and wildcard records, and secure all DNS-management accounts with MFA and auditing.

  • Infoblox identified two unrelated domain-shadowing operations that placed illegal gambling content beneath legitimate school and government domains.
  • Hidden Hawk added individual CNAME records beneath institutional domains, generally pointing the affected hostnames to gambling pages hosted on Cloudflare Pages.
  • A separate operation delegated subzones under maharashtra.gov.in and online.esic.gov.in to ClouDNS nameservers, enabling the operator to manage records beneath those subzones and use a wildcard under gam.maharashtra.gov.in.
  • The primary institutional websites remained available, meaning unauthorized subdomains could evade detection by organizations focused only on their main websites or application logs.
  • The article recommends that DNS operators validate new NS delegations, investigate unexpected subdomains and CNAMEs, review wildcard records, and secure DNS-management accounts with MFA and access-log reviews.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: cloudflare-pages, cloudns, digitalocean, amazon-cloudfront, bunnycdn

Vendors: cloudflare, cloudns, digitalocean, amazon, bunny-net

item.title: ClickFix Brand Abuse, Untested Assets, and AI Agent Security Controls
item.content:encoded:
Window: 26 Oct 07:00 → 26 Oct 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

5 attack chains that started with assets nobody thought to test — Optional

Organizations that focus pentesting only on obvious critical systems can miss overlooked external assets—such as legacy servers, subsidiary platforms, supplier applications, and demos—that provide paths to sensitive data and production controls. The article argues that comprehensive attack-surface discovery and scalable AI-driven testing are needed to identify these hidden attack chains.

  • Research cited by the article found that organizations pentest about 32% of their attack surface on average, leaving roughly two thirds untested.
  • An externally reachable, hostname-less operations server at a transportation company allowed an authentication bypass that exposed live vehicle cargo information and rerouting controls.
  • An outdated analytics server at a global IT services company enabled unauthenticated file reading, disclosure of an administrative password, and a path to a machine in a payment-card environment.
  • A third-party clinical-data application at a pharmaceutical company contained an unauthenticated SQL injection that reached a shared database environment containing 59 databases, including databases of 14 other companies.
  • A public healthcare-platform demo using production application code exposed patient records across four institutions and allowed a low-privilege clinician account to modify records and create non-expiring patient-portal tokens.

Technologies: web-server, database

Products: target-graph, adobe-coldfusion, microsoft-sql-server

Vendors: cycognito, adobe, microsoft

Know How Cyble Brand Intelligence Can Help Stop ClickFix Campaigns in its Tracks — Optional

Cyble argues that its Brand Intelligence & Protection service could disrupt Storm-1865’s Booking.com ClickFix phishing campaign by detecting lookalike domains, cloned phishing pages, and exposed credentials before more hospitality partners are victimized.

  • Microsoft reported that Storm-1865 impersonated Booking.com from December 2024 to target hotel and hospitality staff across North America, Europe, Oceania, and South and Southeast Asia.
  • The campaign used Booking.com-themed emails and PDFs to send victims to fake CAPTCHA pages that instructed them to paste a pre-copied command into the Windows Run box.
  • The command used mshta.exe to retrieve credential- and payment-data-stealing malware, including XWorm, Lumma Stealer, VenomRAT, AsyncRAT, Danabot, and NetSupport RAT.
  • Booking.com stated that its own systems were not breached, although some accommodation partners and customers were affected.
  • The article presents Cyble Brand Intelligence & Protection as a way to identify lookalike domains, cloned phishing pages, brand-related lures, and exposed credentials, while noting it did not participate in the response to this campaign.

Products: cyble-brand-intelligence-and-protection

Vendors: cyble

Deploying AI agents securely: how Kaspersky products mitigate AI threats — Optional

Kaspersky promotes a layered approach to securing enterprise AI agents: discover and restrict them with application and web controls, monitor risky behavior with EDR detections, and scan agent skills and LLM files for malicious code. The article highlights risks such as unsafe auto-approval settings, credential-file access, malicious MCP server artifacts, and untrusted agent extensions.

  • AI agents can access data, run commands, and interact with external services using user privileges, creating security risks when deployed without security-team oversight or well-designed policies.
  • Kaspersky Endpoint Security provides Application Control and Web Control features that organizations can use to restrict AI agent software and access to websites offering AI as a service.
  • Kaspersky EDR includes specialized rules that identify AI agents accessing credential, token, or key files; launching with automatic approval or disabled sandboxing; creating suspicious MCP server files; and unusual applications connecting to external LLM APIs.
  • Kaspersky Threat Intelligence Portal provides AI-agent profiles and Hunt Hub detection rules with information such as system artifacts, audit sources, MITRE ATT&CK mappings, detection logic, and possible false positives.
  • Kaspersky Scan Engine can scan AI-agent skills, associated scripts, agent-generated files, and potentially dangerous LLM model formats for malicious code.

Technologies: edr, antivirus

A Fake China Domain Registry Warns Your CEO About .cn Names — May Read

A phishing scam posing as a Chinese domain registry used an urgent .cn registration warning to lure a UK manufacturer into replying, despite passing SPF, DKIM, and DMARC and containing no malicious links or attachments. The case shows that reply-only social engineering requires behavioral and language-based detection beyond authentication and payload scanning.

  • A UK industrial equipment manufacturer received an urgent email posing as a China domain registration center and claiming that a third party sought to register the company’s name under four .cn-related domains.
  • The email contained no links, attachments, or QR codes beyond a hotlinked signature image, and its intended payload was to induce the recipient to reply.
  • The message passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC because the sender controlled and authenticated its own domain, while Microsoft routed it to Junk with a spam verdict.
  • The sender’s claimed Shanghai registry identity conflicted with records showing a privacy-protected Name.com .net domain, a sending server geolocated to the United States, and a Foxmail client header.
  • IRONSCALES quarantined and automatically resolved the incident as phishing after matching its language and signature pattern to known China domain-registration scam templates.

Products: ironscales-platform, themis, microsoft-365

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft, name-com

item.title: Compromised Microsoft 365 Suppliers Deliver Correlated Aviation RFQ Phishing
item.content:encoded:
Window: 24 Oct 10:00 → 24 Oct 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

One RFQ Number, Two Real Suppliers, 17 Minutes Apart — May Read

Two legitimate aviation suppliers sent near-identical RFQ phishing emails from authenticated Microsoft 365 accounts, revealing a cross-sender campaign only when analysts correlated the shared reference number, template, and landing-page path. Organizations should detect vendor-email compromise by clustering message content and destinations across senders rather than relying solely on sender authentication or reputation.

  • A UK charter airline received two nearly identical RFQ emails numbered 68453 from two different aviation suppliers 17 minutes apart.
  • Both messages were sent from within the suppliers’ Microsoft 365 tenants, passed authentication at the airline’s gateway, and came from first-time senders.
  • Each email used the same template and a bold PDF-named link, while both links resolved to the same aviation-themed path on an unrelated web-design site.
  • Eight mailboxes across two airline domains received the messages, including a fleet support engineer and an engineering director.
  • A human analyst resolved both emails as malicious, and the copies were removed, although the record did not establish whether anyone clicked.

Technologies: email-security

Products: microsoft-365, ironscales-platform

Vendors: microsoft, ironscales

item.title: LiteLLM Secret-Theft Timeline and Python Exposure to CVE-2026-111497
item.content:encoded:
Window: 23 Oct 18:00 → 23 Oct 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

New Evidence Shows LiteLLM Secret-Stealing Workflows Ran 11 Days Before Supply Chain Attack — Must Read

Socket found that attackers ran malicious GitHub Actions workflows in the LiteLLM repository on October 10 and 12, 2026—up to 11 days before the malicious PyPI release—to exfiltrate organization and environment secrets. LiteLLM later linked the stolen GitHub token from the October 10 workflow to approval of the October 21 malicious release.

  • Socket recovered two malicious LiteLLM commits from October 10 and October 12, 2026, that added a GitHub Actions workflow named .github/workflows/cache.yml.
  • The workflows ran from temporary ci-tmp branches that were created and deleted the same day, allowing them to execute without remaining in the repository’s main branch history.
  • The October 10 workflow targeted six organization-level secrets, including GH_TOKEN and a GitHub App private key, while the October 12 workflow targeted 14 additional repository, organization, and environment-scoped secrets.
  • Both workflows encoded collected secrets and sent them to separate webhook.site endpoints, while using error suppression so the GitHub Actions jobs would report success even if transmission failed.
  • LiteLLM stated that its audit logs linked the GH_TOKEN stolen by the October 10 workflow to approval of the malicious October 21, 2026 LiteLLM release.

Technologies: ci-cd, source-control, package-registry, secrets-manager, cloud-platform

Products: litellm, github-actions, github, pypi, gitguardian, linear, aws-bedrock

Vendors: berriai, github, socket, gitguardian, linear, together-ai, openai, amazon-web-services

Python packages are also vulnerable to the Node2Shell Brotli flaw (CVE-2026-111497) — Should Read

Python environments using Brotli 1.2.0 or earlier or brotlicffi 1.2.0.x are vulnerable to CVE-2026-111497, a Brotli decoder memory-safety flaw reachable through compressed HTTP traffic. Upgrade to Brotli 1.2.1 or brotlicffi 1.2.1.0 and rebuild affected environments and container images.

  • CVE-2026-111497 is a Brotli decoder flaw that affects Python packages Brotli 1.2.0 and earlier and brotlicffi 1.2.0.x.
  • The patched releases are Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0.
  • Python applications can reach the vulnerable decoder through malicious Brotli-compressed responses from outbound HTTP requests or Brotli-compressed inbound request bodies.
  • urllib3, requests, httpx, aiohttp, and Scrapy may automatically use Brotli decoding when Brotli or brotlicffi is installed.
  • As of October 23, the article states that pip-audit, Dependabot, and Safety do not flag the affected Python packages because advisory databases have not mapped the CVE to them.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: brotli, brotlicffi, nodejs, urllib3, requests, httpx, aiohttp, scrapy

Vendors: google, nodejs-project, aikido-security
